name: Question 3
worked_solution:
First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)) \\  & =x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{yy}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)) \\  & =-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find ${f}_{yyx}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{yy}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yyx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{yy}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)) \\  & =-2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)-{x}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\cdot y \\  & =-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)-{x}^{2}y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Calculate fyyx(x,y) given that f(x,y)=sin⁡(xy).

a
x2sin⁡(xy)−xycos⁡(xy)
b
x2ycos⁡(xy)
c
−x2ysin⁡(xy)
d
−2xsin⁡(xy)−x2ycos⁡(xy)
e
−xsin⁡(xy)+xycos⁡(xy)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we find the first-order derivative fy(x,y):

fy(x,y)=∂∂y(sin⁡(xy))=xcos⁡(xy)

Next, we find fyy(x,y) by differentiating fy(x,y) with respect to y:

fyy(x,y)=∂∂y(fy(x,y))=∂∂y(xcos⁡(xy))=−x2sin⁡(xy)

Finally, we find fyyx(x,y) by differentiating fyy(x,y) with respect to x:

fyyx(x,y)=∂∂x(fyy(x,y))=∂∂x(−x2sin⁡(xy))=−2x⋅sin⁡(xy)−x2⋅cos⁡(xy)⋅y=−2xsin⁡(xy)−x2ycos⁡(xy)
